title: Caching
summary: Keep frequently reused data closer to the request path.
solves: Repeated expensive reads and latency-sensitive access.
useWhen: The workload has meaningful locality and stale data is tolerable within a defined window.
tradeoff: Invalidation, memory cost, and inconsistency become part of the design.
commonMistake: Adding a cache before stating the key, ownership, eviction, and miss behavior.

title: Replication
summary: Maintain multiple copies of data or service state.
solves: Read scale, fault tolerance, and regional availability.
useWhen: A single copy cannot meet availability or read-throughput goals.
tradeoff: Replication lag and failover coordination complicate consistency.
commonMistake: Assuming replicas are instantly consistent or failover is automatic and lossless.

title: Partitioning
summary: Split a growing dataset or workload across independent owners.
solves: Storage and throughput limits of a single node.
useWhen: A stable partition key can distribute the dominant access pattern.
tradeoff: Cross-partition queries, rebalancing, and hot keys become harder.
commonMistake: Choosing a key without checking skew or future migration.

title: Consistent Hashing
summary: Map keys to a changing set of owners while limiting remapping.
solves: Large-scale redistribution when cache or storage nodes join and leave.
useWhen: Clients or routers need stable key ownership across an elastic node ring.
tradeoff: Virtual-node balance, hotspots, and membership propagation add complexity.
commonMistake: Naming the technique without explaining replicas, skew, or failure ownership.

title: Load Balancing
summary: Distribute requests across healthy service instances.
useWhen: Stateless or appropriately coordinated service replicas can share traffic.
tradeoff: Health checks, connection affinity, and overload policy need explicit handling.
commonMistake: Drawing a load balancer without describing failure detection or routing policy.

title: Queues
summary: Separate work acceptance from work execution.
solves: Traffic bursts, slow downstream work, and independent scaling.
useWhen: The caller does not require synchronous completion.
tradeoff: Duplicates, delay, ordering, and poison messages require policy.
commonMistake: Calling delivery exactly-once without an idempotent consumer design.

title: Pub/Sub
summary: Distribute events to multiple independent subscribers.
solves: Loose coupling between producers and several consumers.
useWhen: Multiple workflows react to the same fact on their own timelines.
tradeoff: Schema evolution, replay, and consumer lag need ownership.
commonMistake: Using pub/sub when a single-owner work queue is the actual requirement.

title: Consistency
summary: Define what different readers may observe after a write.
solves: Ambiguity about correctness across replicas and services.
useWhen: Every design: the required guarantee should follow the user-visible invariant.
tradeoff: Stronger coordination can increase latency or reduce availability during partitions.
commonMistake: Choosing strong or eventual consistency as a slogan instead of per operation.

title: CDN
summary: Serve cacheable content from geographically distributed edges.
solves: Origin load and long-distance delivery latency.
useWhen: Content is public or safely cache-keyed and reused across viewers.
tradeoff: Purge delay, cache keys, and private content boundaries matter.
commonMistake: Treating all API responses as safely cacheable at the edge.

title: Rate Limiting
summary: Bound accepted work by identity, resource, and time window.
useWhen: A service needs an explicit admission-control policy.
tradeoff: Accuracy, availability, memory, and coordination compete at large scale.
commonMistake: Naming an algorithm without defining the key or failure behavior.

title: Idempotency
summary: Make repeated execution produce one intended effect.
solves: Retries after ambiguous failures and duplicate delivery.
useWhen: Clients or queues may repeat a state-changing operation.
tradeoff: Deduplication keys require scope, storage, and expiration.
commonMistake: Assuming HTTP method names alone make business operations idempotent.

title: Retries
summary: Attempt transiently failed work again under a bounded policy.
useWhen: The operation is safe to repeat and the failure is plausibly transient.
tradeoff: Retries amplify overload unless paired with backoff, jitter, and budgets.
commonMistake: Retrying every error immediately and indefinitely.

title: Backpressure
summary: Signal or enforce that producers must slow down.
solves: Queues and consumers being overwhelmed by sustained input.
useWhen: Arrival rate can exceed processing capacity for longer than a brief burst.
tradeoff: The system must decide what to delay, reject, sample, or degrade.
commonMistake: Treating an unbounded queue as a capacity strategy.
